title: Tech Note: Reading a Full SOAP Request

historical_commentary.text: This note documents a low-level, partly undocumented technique (via GET WEB FORM VARIABLES) for reading raw incoming SOAP requests in 4th Dimension's native Web Service publishing system, reflecting the SOAP-centric web-services standard dominant in the early-to-mid 2000s. SOAP-based service publishing has since been broadly superseded industry-wide, and within 4D specifically, by REST APIs (especially via ORDA, introduced 2017+) as the primary way to expose 4D data and logic to external callers, though 4D's classic SOAP publishing commands likely remain available for legacy compatibility.
related_updates: REST APIs (notably via ORDA, 2017+) have become 4D's primary mechanism for publishing data/logic to external callers, superseding SOAP-based publishing for new development

Reliance on undocumented command behavior for reading raw request data, as shown here, is inherently fragile and would be considered poor practice by modern standards; any current equivalent would look for a documented API
